transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

Not necessarily. Damp clothes after a full wash and dry are more often caused by a blocked fluff filter or restricted airflow than a failed heater, and that's especially likely on a machine that isn't very old. From what you have described, the most likely cause is lint filter / airflow restriction (clean first). Next: Clean the lint/fluff filter and (on condenser models) the condenser, and make sure the airflow path isn't restricted. Let me know what you find.
ok, I can do that. No error codes showing on the display, and the drum does get hot during drying. Anything else I should check while I'm at it?
Next: Check the wash actually SPUN and DRAINED the water out - clothes that go into the dry soaking will never dry (that's a wash-side fault). Let me know what you find.
The clothes come out of the wash fine as far as I can tell, but I often turn the spin down to 800 to reduce creasing. I'm not sure if that counts as properly spun. Is that a problem?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. It counts as spun, but 800 leaves noticeably more water in the clothes than a higher spin speed, so the dryer has more moisture to remove. That can contribute to damp results, especially with a fuller load, though on its own it doesn't mean anything is faulty. Next: Try a SMALLER dry load - a washer-dryer dries less than it washes. Let me know what you find.
I tried a half drum with full spin and it came out dry. A full 9kg drum washed and dried in one go is what I normally do, though the manual says 6kg for drying.
Good news, that has sorted it. If it happens again, start with the same check. Is there anything else I can help with?
